# US-02.4 — Tell a supplied zone identity apart from an inferred one

| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-02 Multimodal Perception & Gemini Reasoning](../epics/EPIC-02-multimodal-perception.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                                            |
| **Estimate**     | 2                                                                                             |

| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                               |
| **Files**        | [backend/services/vision_analyzer.py](../../../backend/services/vision_analyzer.py)           |

| **Requirements** | [FR-29, FR-3](../../../agile/requirements.md); resolved OQ-1                                  |

## User story

**As an** urban analyst,
**I want** each zone identity field marked as supplied or inferred,
**so that** I can distinguish authoritative location input from the model's best-effort guess.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Field-level provenance**
Given any combination of supplied and omitted `zone_id`, `zone_name`, `lat` and `lng`,
when analysis succeeds,
then the report identifies each field individually as caller-supplied or model-inferred according to its actual origin.

**AC2 — No model override**
Given valid supplied identity values that conflict with model inference,
when analysis succeeds,
then each supplied value appears verbatim and is marked supplied, while only omitted values may be inferred.

**AC3 — Partial coordinate input**
Given only one valid coordinate component is supplied,
when analysis succeeds,
then that component remains unchanged and supplied while the other is inferred and marked inferred.

**AC4 — Serialized provenance survives consumption**
Given a completed report with mixed identity origins,
when it is serialized and validated against the agreed report contract,
then all four provenance distinctions remain readable without treating inferred values as authoritative measurements.

## Tasks

- [x] Preserve supplied zone strings and a complete coordinates object over model output
- [x] Ask Gemini to infer metadata only when it is absent
- [ ] Agree the serialized provenance representation and align the report schema and validator
- [ ] Merge coordinate components independently instead of replacing the whole object
- [ ] Return and test field-level provenance for all supplied/omitted combinations
- [ ] Coordinate the upload contract with STORY-029 without adding HTTP handling to the analyzer

## Current state

The analyzer currently preserves complete supplied metadata but returns no provenance fields. Its strict schema forbids extra fields. The resolved OQ-1 decision requires provenance per field, not just one report-wide origin.

| Gap                                                                            | Impact                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| No serialized origin for any identity field                                    | Consumers cannot distinguish trusted input from inference                                              |
| `payload.update(metadata)` replaces the entire supplied coordinates object     | A latitude-only or longitude-only input cannot retain the inferred other component                     |
| FR-29 specifies semantics but not a JSON representation in guide section 3     | Schema and validator alignment must be agreed before AC4 can be frozen; do not invent field names here |
| STORY-030 depends on STORY-029, which also depends on STORY-030 in the backlog | Circular dependency blocks sequencing; the orchestrator must resolve it without changing product scope |

OQ-1 is resolved; it must not be reopened as a question about whether caller identity is supported. The remaining clarification is the serialized provenance contract and the existing dependency cycle.

## Test cases

| Test                                                     | Asserts                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_identity_provenance_is_reported_per_field`         | Each of four fields records its actual supplied/inferred origin |
| `test_supplied_identity_cannot_be_overridden_by_model`   | Conflicting model values cannot replace validated input         |
| `test_partial_coordinates_preserve_supplied_component`   | Latitude-only and longitude-only cases merge independently      |
| `test_identity_provenance_survives_report_serialization` | Agreed contract retains provenance after serialization          |

## Definition of done

The provenance representation is agreed, schema and validator accept it, all four criteria pass with mocked Gemini, and STORY-029 can consume the result without losing origin information. Coverage meets the 70% floor and the dependency cycle is resolved by the orchestrator. Estimate 2 is retained; contract agreement is a prerequisite, not silently additional implementation scope.
